name: Hamster Care Checklist
description: A hamster care checklist covering cage setup, bedding, diet, the wheel, cleaning and handling.

items.text: Choose a cage with a large continuous floor area
items.note: Bigger than typical starter cages; secure against escapes

items.text: Position the cage away from drafts, direct sun and noise
Add a hideout or sleeping house
Include a sand bath for grooming
Keep the cage out of reach of other pets
Use deep, dust-free bedding suitable for burrowing
Provide safe nesting material such as plain paper
Avoid pine and cedar shavings
items.note: Their oils can cause respiratory irritation

items.text: Spot-remove soiled and damp bedding daily
Provide a quality hamster food mix or pellets
Offer small amounts of safe fresh vegetables
Give occasional protein or treats in moderation
Supply constant fresh water in a bottle or bowl
Remove uneaten fresh food before it spoils
Provide a correctly sized solid-surface wheel
Add tunnels, chews and climbing items
Offer foraging by scattering some food in bedding
Allow supervised time in a safe exercise area
Provide safe chew toys to manage growing teeth
Spot-clean soiled bedding and the toilet corner daily
Wash the water bottle and food bowl regularly
Clean the wheel and accessories weekly
Do a partial deep clean while preserving some old bedding
Refresh the sand bath as needed
Let a new hamster settle before regular handling
Build trust gradually with calm, low handling
Check teeth, eyes, nose and coat for problems
Watch for wet tail, lethargy or weight loss
Consult a small-animal vet for any health concern

faq.q: What size cage does a hamster need?
faq.a: Hamsters need much more floor space than most starter cages offer, with deep bedding for burrowing. Choose the largest continuous floor area you can, and avoid small wire cages with shallow bases.

faq.q: What should I feed a hamster?
faq.a: Offer a quality hamster mix or pellets as a base, with small amounts of fresh vegetables and occasional protein, plus constant fresh water. Avoid sugary, salty or human junk foods and confirm safe extras for your species.
Yes. A correctly sized, solid-surface wheel lets a hamster run safely each night. The wheel should be large enough that the back stays flat, not arched, and have no rungs or gaps that can trap feet.

faq.q: How do I handle a hamster without stressing it?
faq.a: Let a new hamster settle for a few days, then build trust slowly with a calm voice and treats. Handle gently and low to the ground, and for health or behavior concerns consult a vet familiar with small animals.

faq.q: Can I print this hamster care checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF so you can keep it near the cage and tick off daily and weekly tasks.
